entries.title: Working collaboratively to fight scams in Asia Pacific
entries.summary: A woman using her smartphone, surrounded by graphic icons representing online security, privacy, and message alerts.
entries.content:
Scams are growing more complex, fueled by increasingly sophisticated tactics from transnational crime groups. A recent UN report illustrated the effect these scams have across the Asia Pacific (APAC) region. In 2025, scam losses across East Asia, Southeast Asia, Australia, and New Zealand reached up to $114.1 billion USD, with over 40% of ASEAN consumers said to be experiencing scams.

Tackling these highly organized networks requires a unified effort. Today, we are sharing how, at Google, we are scaling our defenses to protect APAC communities. This includes built-in protections across products and platforms, industry-wide collaboration, and new local partnerships to increase community resilience.

Built-in protections across devices and platforms

Our first line of defense is to secure the devices and platforms people use every day. This year, Android launched Fake Call Detection, a feature designed to spot AI-driven phone call impersonation. Built on open RCS technology, other platforms can adopt the same protections. On Pixel, built-in scam detection now alerts you to potential scams from many popular messaging apps. We are partnering to bring this to additional Android users later this year. We are also expanding Android developer verification to protect people against malicious apps outside Google Play, wherever apps are distributed.

Industry alignment for collective defense

Beyond product solutions, defeating fraud networks requires coordination across experts and industries. Earlier this year, we joined industry peers to sign the Industry Accord Against Online Scams and Fraud, taking a collective approach to sharing threat intelligence and coordinating defenses. Building on the Industry Accord, we recently helped establish the Japan Anti-Scam Alliance (JASA) to enable public and private institutions to deploy aligned defenses.

Google.org also recently helped launch the Global Anti-Scams Philanthropy Collaborative to coordinate cross-industry philanthropic action against scams globally.

Efforts to strengthen community resilience

To strengthen resilience at the community level, today Google.org announced $6 million in funding to The Asia Foundation and the Tech for Good Institute to help small businesses and individuals in APAC to stay safe online. The efforts will include training local communities on building scam resilience, incubating AI-powered defense prototypes, and equipping policymakers with insights to strengthen threat measures.

This builds on Google.org’s ongoing support for local organizations, like Bamboo Builders in Singapore and the Taiwan FactCheck Center, to deliver specialized, hyper-local training to citizens. And it expands on the ASEAN Foundation’s Scam Ready ASEAN initiative, which is bringing online scam prevention resources to millions in the region. We are also expanding Be Scam Ready, an educational scam-awareness game — and one of the Scam Ready ASEAN’s program resources — to Indonesia, Japan, Malaysia, the Philippines, and Vietnam. Be Scam Ready simulates common scams to prepare citizens, and is already available in Singapore, Thailand, and Taiwan.

Helping communities stay ahead of organized fraud is central to our work, and we will continue to advocate for a collaborative, global approach.

entries.title: Advancing research and partnering with universities in Singapore
entries.summary: A light beam is focused through a lens into thin wires that pass through panels featuring increasingly complex patterns of blue dots, dashes, and other geometric shapes. The Google G is on the bottom left corner.
entries.content:
Technology is already transforming how we approach the world’s toughest challenges, and continuing that momentum requires supporting the people driving foundational science. With our newly established research hub in Singapore, and as we continue to scale existing health research initiatives in the country — including bringing open models like MedGemma to frontline care settings — Google is also deepening its academic partnerships in Singapore by investing over $6 million in new research grants and capacity-building initiatives at National University of Singapore (NUS) and Nanyang Technological University (NTU).

Backing foundational and applied breakthroughs

Our targeted grants address both urgent biomedical frontiers and the core building blocks of computing:

  • Alzheimer’s research ($1.5 million grant — NUS): Selected from over 3,500 global applications, NUS has been awarded an AI for Science Google.org Impact Challenge Grant to advance breakthroughs in neurodegenerative disease research using AI models and data science.
  • Computing efficiency and regional languages ($500,000 grant — NUS): This funding supports machine learning efficiency — focusing on sustainable compute and model serving optimization — and regional language processing.
  • AI safety and security ($340,000 grant — NTU): We are funding four sponsored research studies at NTU focused on advancing AI safety frameworks, robust evaluation methodologies, trustworthy multi-agent systems, and privacy-preserving LLM watermarking.

The Google team met with NUS leadership, including Senior Vice Provost Prof. Bernard Tan and Dean of Computing Prof. Tulika Mitra, to align on new research infrastructure and cross-disciplinary workstreams.

Building capacity for research ecosystem and future scholars

Beyond individual research projects, true ecosystem enablement requires investing in long-term institutional infrastructure and talent pipelines.

At NTU, a $750,000 AI for Science Capacity Fund Grant will help build permanent research capabilities across Southeast Asia. Under Professor Ho Teck Hua’s regional academic leadership, this initiative will establish lasting infrastructure, foster internal research agents, and build ethical AI frameworks that elevate the region’s scientific capacity.

Google.org and Google DeepMind are also providing $3 million in funding to support INSEAD’s Thrive Lab in Singapore, which aims to advance global research into how people and organizations can thrive alongside rapid technological change. The lab will explore how education, workplaces, and communities can better support people to develop skills, find purpose, and build meaningful relationships in a changing world.

This human-centered research sits alongside a broader wave of scientific breakthroughs driving the region forward. Whether unlocking insights into neurodegenerative diseases, making models more efficient and inclusive of local languages, or establishing safe research infrastructure, Singapore’s academic community continues to set a global benchmark for innovation. We are proud to enable with our tools and models the faculty, researchers, and students who are not just experimenting with AI, but preparing to lead the next era of scientific progress

The Google team met with the NTU Deputy President & Provost, Prof Christian Wolfrum and colleagues to discuss partnerships across frontier research and AI safety, science, and education.

entries.title: The latest AI news we announced in October 2026
entries.summary: Animated carousel of images from AI posts in October
entries.content:
For more than 20 years, we’ve invested in machine learning and AI research, tools, and infrastructure to build products that make everyday life better for more people. Teams across Google are working on ways to unlock AI’s benefits in fields as wide-ranging as healthcare, crisis response, and education. To keep you posted on our progress, we're doing a regular roundup of Google's most recent AI news.

Here’s a look back at some of our AI announcements from October.

October underscored our commitment to AI innovation, as we released one frontier model globally and announced our next one just two weeks later. After rolling out Gemini 4 Argon — a frontier reasoning model — to developers, enterprises, scientists, and consumers, we announced Gemini 4 Carbon, our strongest model yet for long-horizon engineering and cybersecurity defense. Carbon illustrates the pace at which we’re pushing the frontier forward while strengthening our safety guardrails in tandem. Elsewhere in October, we introduced Genie 4 for real-time interactive world simulation with native audio, unveiled our smartest fitness tracker with Google Fitbit Edge, broke open a 20-year bottleneck in quantum computing, and more.

Put Gemini 4 Argon to work today, and see what’s next for Gemini 4 at the frontier. Following early safety testing, Gemini 4 Argon rolled out globally for complex coding, financial analysis, and legal workflows across Google AI Studio, the Gemini API, Google Cloud, Search, and the Gemini app, while also powering physical-world reasoning through Gemini 4 Argon for Robotics. Showing how quickly we’re pushing the frontier forward, two weeks later we announced Gemini 4 Carbon, our strongest model yet with state-of-the-art cybersecurity and long-horizon capabilities. Just as we did with Argon, we’re taking a deliberate approach to rollout: Carbon is now in pre-release testing with the U.S. government and a subset of trusted cyber defenders via the Fairwind Program as we refine safety guardrails and expand partner testing ahead of a broader launch to developers, businesses, and consumers.

Step into real-time interactive worlds with Genie 4. Genie 4 brings unprecedented realism, advanced physics, lifelike human movement, and native audio to real-time interactive simulation. You can steer scenes as they unfold using natural language. Genie 4 advances on our ability to create safe training environments for robots and AI agents as a crucial step toward AGI. Explore the demos on the Google DeepMind blog.

Verify AI-generated content more easily around the world. Having already watermarked more than 180 billion images and videos and 240,000 years of audio with SynthID, we’re expanding SynthID Detector globally in English so anyone can check whether an image, video, or audio clip was generated with AI. Alongside built-in verification tools in Search, Chrome, and the Gemini app that regularly handle over a million requests each day, SynthID Detector also identifies AI content from industry partners like OpenAI, NVIDIA, Kakao, and Apple.

Stay protected from mobile scams with new Android safeguards. AI-powered Scam Detection in Phone by Google and Google Messages already flags more than 5 million suspected scam calls and texts every month. Now, Android is introducing an opt-in Enhanced protection mode in Google Messages that uses Private AI Compute and our latest cloud Gemini models to catch sophisticated conversational scams, paired with expanded chat alerts and stronger call-forwarding and screen-sharing defenses.

Meet Google Fitbit Edge, our all-new smartest fitness tracker ever. Available now in a slim, comfortable design with up to seven days of battery life 1 , Fitbit Edge 2 pairs precision GPS and automatic workout recognition across 50+ activities with personalized guidance from the Gemini-powered Google Health Coach 3 We also rolled out more than 55 updates across Google Health and Fitbit Air, including effortless photo meal logging, new Metal Mesh bands, and Health Guardian features that monitor long-term blood pressure and insulin resistance trends 4 .

See how AI could improve patient-physician relationships in clinical care. In Google’s first publication in the main journal of The Lancet, researchers from Google and Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center evaluated our AMIE conversational medical AI system during real-world primary care clinic visits. By gathering patient histories and generating clinical summaries before urgent care appointments, AMIE helped clinicians prepare in 75% of cases and matched doctors’ final differential diagnoses 90% of the time. This is part of our broader work applying AI to better understand, detect, and treat disease.

Create and play custom games in Playground. Our new experimental gaming platform lets anyone build, remix, and share custom single- and multiplayer games from simple text prompts with zero coding required. That same no-code creativity is expanding across our platforms: Android users can now build personal AI apps with Google AI Studio and install them directly on their phones through Google Play, and music producers can vibe code custom instruments and audio plugins in Google Flow Music.

Celebrate educators and sharpen your learning. For World Teachers’ Day, teachers from around the globe shared how they use Gemini to personalize lessons and spark critical thinking, alongside a new global idea search launched in partnership with TED. Whether you’re in the classroom or preparing for a big project, you can also study smarter with Gemini Notebook using interactive learning overviews and custom quizzes, and use new co-creation controls to shape your Slide Decks and Video Overviews before they generate.

Build privacy-first multimodal search with EmbeddingGemma 2. Engineered on the Gemma 4 architecture with 740 million parameters, our new open embedding model moves beyond text to map code, images, video, and audio into a single unified space right on everyday devices. Its modular design cuts local vector storage by up to 6x, making it easy for developers to build private, offline apps that can find a specific video clip from a voice memo or search hours of audio with a text query.

Read the first AI response beamed back from our Project Suncatcher satellite. After launching TPUs into low-Earth orbit, our first Project Suncatcher prototype satellite returned the first-ever AI response generated by a data center-class Google TPU in space: a haiku composed onboard by Gemma 4. This milestone confirms our hardware survived launch and can run AI workloads in orbit. Our team will continue to test how the chips handle radiation and thermal extremes while harnessing space’s abundant solar energy as part of a long-term moonshot toward scalable orbital AI infrastructure.

See how our latest research is accelerating scientific discovery. At our annual Research@ 2026 event, we shared new ways we’re putting advanced AI in the hands of scientists and experts — including demonstrating an experimental Geospatial Reasoning agent, opening public access to our Deep Review tool for technical papers, and delivering top-ranked flu hospitalization forecasting. These breakthroughs are part of a broader, company-wide effort to push the boundaries of scientific discovery. Beyond the event, Google teams are also advancing planetary research by mapping the world’s forest types, while Google.org has awarded $36 million to 17 organizations accelerating scientific breakthroughs with AI.

See how we broke open a 20-year bottleneck in quantum computing. In a landmark study published in Science, Google Quantum AI demonstrated that a technique called "magic state cultivation" works in practice on our Willow quantum processor, cutting errors roughly 40-fold compared to uncultivated states. Because producing high-purity magic states previously threatened to consume up to 95% of a quantum computer’s resources, this breakthrough clears a major hurdle on the path to large-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computers.

entries.title: Google Messages, Phone by Google, and Google Contacts get new, updated icons.
entries.summary: Google is updating the icons for Messages, Phone, and Contacts with a sleeker, cohesive design. See the new look for your home screen.
entries.content:
Starting today, we’re rolling out refreshed icons for three apps that help you stay connected: Google Messages, Phone by Google, and Google Contacts.

These are the same apps you trust and use every day, now with enhanced icons designed with your feedback in mind. The new icons are sharper and clearer on your home screen. For example, we’ve added a subtle but crisp gradient with easily readable edges. They also feature updated curvature and coloring to align with the rest of the Google apps you know and love, such as our core Google logo.

Don’t worry, the functionality of these apps isn’t changing as a result of the new icons. You’ll simply spot a sleeker, more cohesive look on your home screen in the coming weeks.

Check out the conversation on our community forum for more.

entries.title: We’ve received our first response from the Project Suncatcher prototype satellite.
entries.summary: Video showing the Project Suncatcher team explaining the project and reacting to the TPU-generated haiku
entries.content:
On October 1, we launched our prototype satellite for Project Suncatcher. The launch marked the first step in our long-term research moonshot to explore powering AI compute in space. Since then, we've spent the last few weeks completing our commissioning checklist, which included powering up the host and TPU trays and successfully running early machine learning tests. This week, we reached our "Hello World" milestone: the first-ever AI response from a data center class TPU in orbit.

During a ground-station pass, we uplinked our first prompt to our onboard Gemma 4 open model, asking it to generate a haiku about being in space. As the satellite passed by Svalbard, Norway, the downlinked poem confirmed success:

Blue marble below

Data streams in silent grace

Starlight feeds my core. ✨

Following this initial output, we tested space-themed limericks and telemetry prompts reporting the technical status of the payload systems. Next, we will continue with a series of tests to evaluate how TPUs perform under thermal stress and radiation exposure in orbit. Verifying our TPUs can reliably execute workloads in space paves the way for our next milestone of twin interconnected satellites in 2027.

Our chips have officially earned their space wings — an important achievement on the long road ahead for this cosmic moonshot.

entries.title: See who has access to your Gmail inbox in 2 minutes.
entries.summary: Run a quick Google Security Checkup and protect your email with three quick and easy steps.
entries.content:
When’s the last time you checked who (or what) has access to your Gmail inbox? Run a quick Google Security Checkup and protect your email with three quick and easy steps:

  • Review signed-in devices.
  • Remove old third-party app access.
  • Confirm recovery information.

For more ways to keep your inbox safe from phishing and unwanted senders, check out the Gmail Help Center guide on protecting your account.

entries.title: You can now generate, preview, and edit documents, PDFs, presentations, spreadsheets, and more directly in Gemini.
entries.summary: Generate, edit, and preview PDFs or Docs directly in Gemini. Use the new full-screen editor to refine your files today. See what's new in Gemini.
entries.content:
We’re introducing new ways to create and refine documents, PDFs, presentations, spreadsheets, code, and more in the Gemini app.

You can now generate, preview, and edit files right within your chat — expand to full screen to type edits directly, highlight text to ask questions, or have Gemini refine your files. PDF preview and editing is supported on both the web and mobile, while all other formats (Google Docs, Google Sheets, slide decks, Markdown files, TXT files, and code) are supported on the web only.

As shown in the video below, you can now ask Gemini to create a PDF study guide from your uploaded handwritten lecture notes and then you can easily manually edit, highlight specific sections to have Gemini make edits to text or visuals, and even ask further questions.

These capabilities are now available to all users in all languages where Gemini app is available.

entries.title: Colorado students joined a Google hackathon to tackle energy grid challenges.
entries.summary: Students at the Google Colorado Impact Hackathon built AI tools like SolarSnap to modernize the energy grid. See the winning innovations here.
entries.content:
We held the second annual Colorado Impact Hackathon at our Boulder offices, in partnership with CU Boulder and the Colorado Energy Office.

Participating students tackled a crucial challenge: How can we create a clean, secure, and resilient electric grid in Colorado? The winning projects addressed this head on:

  • First place: SolarSnap, an AI app that helps homeowners find the ideal setup for solar panels using their phone’s camera
  • Second place: Grid Watch, an AI-managed battery network designed to keep power on during wildfire shutoffs while reducing electricity costs.
  • Third place: Grid Guard, providing predictive capabilities for targeted grid hardening

At the event, Colorado Attorney General Phil Weiser and CU Boulder Vice Chancellor for Sustainability Andrew Mayock highlighted the importance of bold innovation to shape Colorado’s clean energy future.

From mitigating wildfire risks to tackling energy backlogs, events like these demonstrate how collaboration between students, public leaders, and technologists can drive meaningful change for Colorado.

entries.title: Gemini Notebook makes hundreds of textbooks available to help students learn even more.
entries.summary: Add textbooks from OpenStax and S Chand to Google Gemini Notebook. Generate custom study guides and quizzes now. See the available catalog.
entries.content:
Last month, we introduced Expert Intelligence, a cross-Google initiative that helps you engage with your trusted sources through Google AI products. While you can already add eligible ebooks purchased from Google Play Books, today we’re expanding that experience so students can easily add materials for their courses.

Students can now access hundreds of textbooks from providers in the U.S. and India including OpenStax, Open Textbook Library, and S Chand Publishing, right in Gemini Notebook at no charge. Once you add a textbook, every answer is grounded directly in the textbook, with inline citations and direct links back to the original source. Gemini Notebook also lets you transform textbook content into tailored study guides, practice quizzes, flashcards, and more.

To explore and add these textbooks, select “Add sources” within your notebook and select “Textbooks” to see the available catalog.
